summary: Design the configurable display frame-rate bound (OWNER_RULINGS §M) against v3-broker + v3-dispsw-exp; read-only, reviewed

investigations.summary:
The KMS-flip lens of §M, read at origin/v3-broker c38032f3 merged in my head with origin/v3-dispsw-exp 86b4fa10. The vblank emulation and EDID code that matters is on master/v3-broker. v3-dispsw-exp does not touch kf-qemu/src/display.rs or kf-disp/src/engine.rs (its kf-disp change is model.rs only).

Today the vblank is a deadline in the kf3-display worker's epoll loop, not a timerfd. Its period comes only from the raster the guest programmed. Non-tearing window flips park until that tick, and their completions also wait for the scanout copy. So pacing ordinary vsync'd KMS flips is a one-line clamp: tick period = max(raster period, 1/bound). The clamp lives entirely on the worker thread: no vCPU path changes and no lock is held while waiting.

The bound is NOT exact in three places today:
- Tearing (IMMEDIATE / async) flips, which latch without a tick.
- Copies the worker makes without a flip: the fixed 30 Hz/4 Hz refresh clock, and immediate recomposes on cursor moves.
- The EDID. It still advertises 60 Hz modes that NVKMS accepts even when the EDID's own range excludes them. Above about 71 Hz, the 1080p mode does not fit the DVI single-link 165 MHz clock.

The broker's EV_FRAME credit and demand signals are downstream and must stay that way. The status line carries only cumulative counters: no rate and no bound.

It is worth testing whether the clamp bounds X11 vsync too. Guest NVKMS vblank callbacks, including vblank-semaphore control, run off kf-disp's tick. A display-max-fps=30 run with x11-dispsw=on would show it.

Nothing was edited. Branch trees were exported read-only to the scratchpad at /tmp/claude-0/-workspace-nvidia-gpu-passthrough/85f9c0ab-d91a-47ab-b068-c099d453dd8f/scratchpad/{brk,dsw}.
findings: WHERE THE VBLANK IS EMULATED TODAY. The thread is `kf3-display` (crates/kf-qemu/src/ffi_unsafe.rs:172-174, running Device::display_loop at display.rs:1502). The timer is that loop's epoll deadline, not a timerfd (display.rs:25-26). Each pass takes the minimum of the next per-head vblank, a 2 ms acquire poll, the refresh clock and 50 ms (display.rs:1593-1616). Each head's period is stored in `next_vblank` (display.rs:1568). It is (re)armed from Effect::Heads (display.rs:2032-2064), which the engine emits whenever the armed head set changes (engine.rs:926-928). On a tick, step 4 (display.rs:1750-1787) does four things: it calls engine.vblank(head), which latches the groups parked for that head (engine.rs:588-596); it writes RG_DPCA FRM_CNT and the LOADV counter; it raises HEAD_TIMING LAST_DATA|VBLANK; and it sets `raised` so the interrupt goes out at step 8 (display.rs:2087-2092). Ticks are scheduled drift-free at t+period; if a tick is more than one period late, the timer re-phases from now (display.rs:1764-1768). Precision is per millisecond: PollTimeout::Millis with .max(1) (display.rs:1612-1616; kf-linux-raw/src/epoll_unsafe.rs:52-60). There is deliberately no timerfd (kf-linux-raw/src/lib.rs:239-244). So the AVERAGE rate is exact and each tick jitters by up to ~1 ms. V3_DISPLAY.md §4.5 (:638) still says 'host timerfd'; that text is stale.

THE RATE SOURCE IS THE GUEST'S RASTER, WITH NO CLAMP. Engine::heads_armed computes period = raster_w × raster_h / pixel clock, applying 1000/1001 when ADJ1000DIV1001 is set, from the ARMED core state (engine.rs:1058-1091, HeadMode at :159-168). Measured on the box: CVT-RB 1024x695@60 gave `head 3 ACTIVE raster 1184x715 period 16680 us` (59.95 Hz; broker_20261003/brkA/run_brkA_qemu_excerpt.log:52) and vblanks=7171 (:116). M1/M2 measured flips at 59.98 / 60.01 Hz (V3_DISPLAY.md:236-245). Nothing caps the period. A custom mode (NVKMS NoVertRefreshCheck) or a hostile guest kernel can program any clock. Ticks are then limited only by the 1 ms poll floor, about 1 kHz per head, each one raising an interrupt when the guest enabled it. MINIMAL CHANGE: add a pure, tested helper in kf-disp: `paced_period_ns(raster_ns, bound_mhz) = if raster_ns == 0 {0} else {max(raster_ns, ceil(1e12/bound_mhz))}`. Apply it where Effect::Heads arms next_vblank (display.rs:2038-2048). Also compare the stored period against the CLAMPED value at :2041; otherwise every Heads effect re-phases the timer. Leave heads_armed truthful: period_ns > 0 is also the 'head lit' predicate at engine.rs:836, :940, display.rs:1800, :1813 and :2187. Log the line as `period X us (raster Y us, bound Z Hz)` at display.rs:2055-2062.

NON-TEARING KMS FLIPS ARE ALREADY TICK-PACED, so clamping the tick makes the bound exact for them. Engine::group_ready parks a group at its head's vblank only when a member is a Window with SET_PRESENT_CONTROL BEGIN_MODE == NON_TEARING on an active head, and the group has no core channel (engine.rs:816-863, test at :829-843). Until the tick, the channel's GET stays before the UPDATE (engine.rs:13-15). After the latch, the Latched effect sets the scanout barrier, and every notifier, release, AWAKEN and GET waits for that copy (display.rs:1898-1916, :1932). Once the clamp is in, everything driven by vblank or flip completion follows the bound: flip-complete/AWAKEN (hence DRM flip events), guest NVKMS vblank callbacks, and the RG_DPCA frame counter. The vCPU side is unchanged: a PUT is one atomic plus an eventfd (display.rs:1238-1243). The model lock is held only to take statements (display.rs:1624-1628). Pacing is a later epoll deadline, never a sleep in a trap or under a lock, which satisfies THE_CONSTRAINTS.md:79-83 and the no-blocking-under-a-lock invariant (:875).

⚠ ASYNC/TEARING FLIPS BYPASS THE TICK, so §M's 'exact on KMS flips' does not hold for them. nvidia-drm 580 enables async_page_flip (ogkm-580 kernel-open/nvidia-drm/nvidia-drm-drv.c:386-388). It maps DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_ASYNC to tearing=TRUE and minPresentInterval=0 (nvidia-drm-crtc.c:1656-1667), and NVKMS then programs BEGIN_MODE_IMMEDIATE (src/nvidia-modeset/src/nvkms-evo3.c:3944-3960). kf-disp's engine sets park=None for anything that is not NON_TEARING (engine.rs:831-843), so such flips latch at once. They are bounded only by one scanout copy in flight (display.rs:1928); brkA measured scanout_avg_us=341 (run_brkA_qemu_excerpt.log:116), so the ceiling is roughly 1-3k flips/s, each costing a host GPU compose. OWNER QUESTION: does the bound cap guest frame production, which means gating tearing flips, or only vsync'd presentation, which means reporting tearing flips separately? If it is a cap, the minimal gate is a pure engine change: keep a per-head last-latch time; an IMMEDIATE window flip on an active head that arrives less than one bound period after that latch parks for that head's next (clamped) tick. Slower async flips still latch immediately and tear as asked. No new timer is needed.

HOW THE GUEST LEARNS THE REFRESH RATE: only from the EDID of kayfabe's virtual DVI-D monitor. The connector is DVI-D on SOR i, protocol SINGLE_TMDS_A, EDID served over SPECIFIC_GET_EDID_V2 (kf-disp/src/model.rs:15-17), with a 165 MHz PCLK_LIMIT (model.rs:893-904). The default monitor is CEA 1080p60 (edid.rs:161-169, built by kf-rm/src/display.rs:125-127 and model_for at :132-138). With the broker, the SURFACE packet carries the host window's refresh in w0 (mHz) (kf3.h:64; conn.rs:1684-1693). That flows through kf3.c:962-973 → dpy_set_ui_info → kf3_ui_info (kf3.c:747-753) → request_ui (display.rs:1325-1337) → apply_ui_request (display.rs:2105-2133) → Monitor::for_window, then a hotplug. for_window maps 0 to 60 Hz and clamps to 24..=75 Hz (edid.rs:178-209). The guest then picks a mode, NVKMS programs the pixel clock and raster, and engine.rs:1058-1091 derives the tick from them. The GOP option ROM embeds the SAME first monitor's EDID (crates/kf-qemu/src/gop.rs:39-91; kf-rm display.rs:118-123: 'the two statements … cannot disagree'). So a configured rate must reach kf_rm::display::monitors() itself, not just the model. ⚠ The relay deduplicates SURFACE on size only (conn.rs:1687-1690), so a refresh-only change on the host never re-authors the guest monitor.

HOW A CONFIGURABLE RATE CHANGES THE EDID. Minimal: monitors(bound) builds the preferred mode as Monitor::for_window(1920, 1080, bound_mhz, 165_000), keeping CEA 1080p60 when the bound is 60. apply_ui_request (display.rs:2116) passes min(SURFACE mHz or 60 Hz, bound). The range-limits descriptor's max vertical rate becomes the bound (it is hard-coded 24..75 at edid.rs:259-263). ⚠ When the bound is below 60, the 60 Hz extras must be dropped: established 640x480/800x600/1024x768@60 (edid.rs:241-243), standard timings @60 (:244-257) and the second 1080p60 DTD (:271-279). NVKMS keeps any EDID-listed mode even when the EDID's own range excludes it ('The EDID … contradicts itself … ignoring VertRefresh check', nvkms-modepool.c:1432-1497, :1472-1490). The tick clamp still holds the bound, but the guest would believe its mode runs at 60 Hz. ⚠ ABOVE ~71 Hz: 1080p CVT-RB is 164.75 MHz at 71 Hz and 167.25 MHz at 72 Hz (computed with edid.rs:84-126's formula). Past 71 Hz, for_window shrinks the SIZE to fit the 165 MHz clock (edid.rs:186-198); at 75 Hz the result is 1800x1012. That is a latent bug on today's broker branch for any 72-75 Hz host, independent of §M. Options: (a) the EDID rate = min(bound, 75, the highest rate at which the requested size fits), so size wins; or (b) a dual-link/HDMI connector, which is a bigger change (model.rs:916-931 declares single-link TMDS).

THE BROKER INTERPLAY: the broker must never pace the guest, and it does not today. EV_FRAME is a host-compositor credit for COMMITs only (proto.h:53-56; conn.rs:25-27, :1695-1701, with a 100 ms backstop). An untaken older frame is simply dropped (display.rs:447-450), and the guest is never held (V3_DISPLAY.md:2263; E3 SIGSTOP of the broker for ~7 s left the guest alive, broker_20261003/brkA2_brkA3/runA3.log:118). The 'two demand signals' — note_demand / note_broker_demand (display.rs:460-465, :503-513, :567-581; ffi_unsafe.rs:728-733; V3_DISPLAY.md:2371-2373) — select only the refresh clock (33 ms vs 250 ms) and whether to make a D2H copy (display.rs:2784-2792). The vblank deadline has no demand term (display.rs:1593-1599). That is correct, because a monitor does not slow down when unwatched. With §M the two compose as min(bound, host credit) for what the host shows, while the guest sees exactly the bound. The only host→guest refresh channel is the SURFACE mHz. When display-max-fps is unset, 'the monitor's refresh' follows it, so the worker caches bound = cfg.unwrap_or(current monitor's preferred refresh_mhz), refreshed in apply_ui_request, which already holds the model lock at display.rs:2111-2120. Nothing new is taken per tick.

⚠ FRAMES MADE WITHOUT A FLIP ARE NOT BOUND BY THE TICK. The refresh clock for front-buffer rendering is fixed at 33 ms when anyone wants frames and 250 ms otherwise (display.rs:2453-2467, firing at :1925-1927). That is 30 Hz regardless of the vblank or any bound. A cursor Update latches immediately: its group has no non-tearing window (engine.rs:551-586 → :843). In off and grab modes every pass with a move sets scan.want (display.rs:1891-1897), and a cursor-mode switch does the same (:1887-1890). Only one copy in flight limits those copies (:1928). §O's 'frames are coalesced to the display rate (§M)' is therefore NOT built. MINIMAL: copies started for a non-flip reason (refresh, cursor move, mode switch) wait until scan.last + bound_period, as one more term in the deadline min at display.rs:1603-1605. The refresh period becomes max(33 ms, bound period), so it never exceeds the bound. Raising it to the bound on a watched console would double idle compose work at 60 Hz; that is a cost decision. Flip-driven copies stay immediate, since they are already tick-paced.

WHAT THE STATUS LINE REPORTS TODAY: cumulative counts only, no rate and no bound. disp[writes puts methods updates notifies releases vblanks irqs …] (device.rs:2258-2276) is followed by broker[sent gpucopy releases blocked backstops …] (broker.rs:259-266). The drainer prints the line every 2 s when it changes (device.rs:1947-1953), and kf3.c prints it at realize and exit (:1283-1298). `updates` counts every UPDATE, core and cursor included (display.rs:2084), so it is not a flip count. The per-head period appears only once, when the head is armed (display.rs:2055-2062). MINIMAL: the worker counts non-tearing window latches on active heads and IMMEDIATE latches separately. Once per second it publishes milli-rates to atomics, and status_line reads them without a lock: `fps[bound=60.000 tick=59.95 kms=59.9 kms_max=60.0 tearing=0 refresh=30 over=0]`. Here `over` is the number of 1 s windows above bound plus tolerance, so a bound that does not hold stays visible even in the exit line. The X11 lens would add its own path fields to the same fragment.

CROSS-LENS, worth one box run: the tick clamp may bound X11 vsync too. Guest NVKMS vblank callbacks are driven by kf-disp's tick: it raises the HEAD_TIMING VBLANK event and the interrupt (display.rs:1782-1786; V3_DISPLAY.md:575, :600-601). Those callbacks write NVKMS vblank-semaphore control, honoring swap interval (ogkm-580 nvkms-vblank-sem-control.c:66-113, registered at :116-147). The dispsw runs measured vsync GL at 59.2-60 FPS while host CPU-RM's release path was entered 0 times and 0x90720101 was never sent (traces/v3_display/dispsw_20261003/README.md:61, :74-75, :102, :147); the README calls the vblank pacing an INFERENCE. A run with display-max-fps=30 and x11-dispsw=on would settle it, grading bare-X windowed and composited glxgears vsync. If they follow 30, those clients need no doorbell lever. Counter-evidence to keep in view: brkA3 on v3-broker, without display-SW, ran glxgears at 82.5 FPS (runA3.log:118; that run's head period was not logged). If kf-disp ever services NOTIFY_ON_VBLANK, step 4 (display.rs:1750-1787) at the clamped tick is the natural place.

PROPERTY PLUMBING AND ABI. Both branches put their realize word in kf3_realize's 8th slot: display_broker on v3-broker at ABI 12 (kf3.h:23, :71-74; kf3.c:1147) and x11_dispsw on v3-dispsw-exp at ABI 13 (dsw kf3.h:19, :45-47; kf3.c:799). Merging them already needs a new ABI (14) carrying both words. display-max-fps should ride that bump as one u32 in mHz, with 0 meaning 'follow the monitor', matching the mHz units of refresh_mhz, SURFACE w0 and ui_request (edid.rs:52-60; display.rs:1019-1021). It then flows through the QEMU property (kf3.c ~:1330-1347) → kf3_realize → Config (device.rs:33-62) → kf_rm::display::monitors(bound), which feeds both GOP (device.rs:263-267) and model_for, and → DisplayPlane::build (device.rs:669-676), whose worker caches the bound. Status: V3_DISPLAY.md:2626-2627 records that display-max-fps is NOT built on any branch.

ORDERED MINIMAL CHANGE for the KMS path: (1) the tested kf-disp helper paced_period_ns, applied at display.rs:2038-2048, which makes non-tearing flips exact; (2) monitors(bound) plus the min with SURFACE mHz in apply_ui_request, plus range-limit max V = bound and 60 Hz extras emitted only when 60 ≤ bound, with tests in edid.rs; (3) the non-flip copy gate in the deadline min and the refresh clock never above the bound; (4) the fps[...] status fragment with `over`; (5) behind the owner's answer, the IMMEDIATE-flip rate gate in Engine::group_ready. All of it runs on the kf3-display worker. The bench grade is kfdisp_probe flip_hz ≈ bound at 30/50/60, plus an async-flip client checked against the `tearing` field.

investigations.summary:
Short answer: with x11-dispsw=on, windowed GLX and X11 Vulkan FIFO were not released by the host. They were paced by kf-disp's own 60 Hz vblank timer, which reaches the guest as a vblank interrupt. Three things show this. (1) On the bare X server (no compositor), kf-disp did zero flips while windowed glxgears ran. Over its whole 12 s life (run 10, qemu.log 9672→9963) `updates` stayed at 3219, while `irqs` rose by 682 (≈60.5/s) with `vblanks`. That is the guest servicing every vblank interrupt, and it ran at 59.5 FPS. The same pattern holds for bare-X vkcube FIFO (10652→11427: updates stuck at 3888, irqs +495 ≈ 8.2 s for 480 frames, so ≈58-59 FPS inferred) and again in run 8. (2) The interrupts switch on when the GL client's display-SW twins are created and off when they are freed. The bare X server holding its own twins did not switch them on (irqs +1/+0). With the switch off (runs 7 and 9), the boot's total `irqs` is 172 against ≈8,600 when on. (3) Nothing else ran at 60 Hz. The host is headless, and host CPU-RM's release path was entered 0 times while the probe's positive control counted 1,983,923 event drains. A headless head has no vblank clock: RM runs such a callback "now" (ogkm-580 vblank.c:209-243), which would give an uncapped rate, not 60. 0x90720101 was never sent: no `GSP REFUSED` line names it, and no code handles it.

This contradicts the premise of OWNER_RULINGS §M (lines 369-371) that vsync'd X11 clients run uncapped on a headless host: vsync gave 59.2-59.8 FPS against 2716 with vsync off. Which guest component consumes the interrupt is not identified. It is handled inside the guest's own RM and never reaches kayfabe; the GET_VBLANK_COUNTER keepalive and NVKMS callbacks are candidates. The attribution is therefore a correlation until the falsifier run below is done.

The lever that works for this stack is kf-disp's vblank period. One knob covers KMS flips, fullscreen X flips and windowed X11 GL/Vulkan FIFO. It is set by the display worker's own poll deadline, so it never blocks a vCPU in a trap and holds no lock. The other levers:
- **NOTIFY_ON_VBLANK:** no measured client uses it.
- **Delaying a host-side release:** there is nothing to delay, and kayfabe has no hook inside host RM or GSP.
- **Pacing doorbells:** I'd not build it. It is leaky (the host twin reads GP_PUT from the guest's own USERD), it conflicts with the inline-doorbell ruling and the fast path, it is too broad (it would also slow the X server's and the compositor's channels), and doorbells per frame vary from 1.9 to 4 by path.

Before any of this is promised, the decisive check is to change kf-disp's refresh (for example to 30 or 50 Hz through the existing request_ui → EDID path) and see whether windowed glxgears and vkcube FIFO follow.

Two further points:
- A front-buffer X11 window with no compositor reaches the host only at kf-disp's fixed copy clock: 30 Hz while the console or broker is watched, 4 Hz otherwise. That was ≈4 Hz in run 10 for a 59.5 FPS client. The status line has to show this rate separately.
- A host GPU that drives a monitor on head 0 is untested. The twin is authored to head 0, so the host's own vblank could add a second wait.
findings: WHAT PACED IT (windowed, bare X, no compositor): kf-disp's vblank interrupt to the guest, not flips and not the host. Run 10 (traces/v3_display/dispsw_20261003/10_b_on_d84086df/run_fin_on_d84086df_qemu.log on origin/v3-dispsw-exp): glxgears' display-SW twin is created at line 9701 and freed at 9865. The status lines that bracket its life (9672→9963) show `updates` stuck at 3219, `irqs` 6717→7399 (+682 ≈ 60.5/s over ~11.3 s) and `vblanks` +729, and glxgears printed 59.45/59.59 FPS (lane.log:162). Run 8 (run_fin_on_c1cc4482_qemu.log) repeats it: irqs +95/120/122/123/120/102 per 2 s with updates +0. Code: the timer tick (origin/v3-dispsw-exp crates/kf-qemu/src/display.rs:1427-1463; origin/v3-broker display.rs:1750-1786) latches flips (engine.vblank), writes the RG_DPCA frame counter, raises HEAD_TIMING VBLANK, and interrupts the guest only if the guest enabled it (kf-disp ports.rs:229-236 status & enable; delivery display.rs:2086-2092 broker / 1737 dispsw). The status line prints every 2 s (device.rs:1947 broker / 1926 dispsw).

X11 VULKAN FIFO is paced the same way: bare-X `vkcube --c 480 --present_mode 2` (hook.sh:217) ran from qemu.log 10652 to 11427 with `updates` stuck at 3888 and `irqs` +495 (≈8.2 s), so 480 frames in ≈8.2 s is ≈58-59 FPS (inferred). The hook records only RC=0, which under `timeout 12` proves only ≥40 FPS. Run 8 shows the same window (irqs +73/121/121/120/60, updates +0).

ON vs OFF is the interrupt clock. The guest turns vblank interrupts on only while a vsync client lives. The bare X server alone, holding its own 4 twins, shows irqs +1/+0 (run 10 status lines just before 9672). Whole-boot totals: run 9 (off) irqs=172 against vblanks=12103; run 10 (on) irqs=8581 against vblanks=13649; run 7 (off) 172; run 8 (on) 8620. Throughout run 9's bare-X glxgears, irqs stayed flat at 165 (qemu.log 7523-8786).

HOST RM DID NOT RELEASE ANYTHING, AND A HEADLESS HOST HAS NO 60 Hz CLOCK. `DSW_TRACE_TOTALS dsw_calls=0 … drains=1983923 drain_client_lookups=0` (10_b_on_d84086df/lane.log:172). CPU-RM has no software methods for the class (ogkm-580 src/nvidia/generated/g_dispsw_nvoc.h:450-452), so GSP firmware services them; a GSP-requested release would enter _kgspRpcSemaphoreScheduleCallback → dispswReleaseSemaphoreAndNotifierFill (src/nvidia/src/kernel/gpu/gsp/kernel_gsp.c:1109-1135; src/nvidia/src/kernel/disp/disp_sw.c:129-178), and it never did. On a head with no vblank interrupt RM runs the callback immediately (src/nvidia/src/kernel/gpu/disp/vblank_callback/vblank.c:87-90, 209-243), which would give an uncapped rate, not 60.

0x90720101 (NOTIFY_ON_VBLANK) IS NOT IN THE MEASURED STACK. It is ROUTE_TO_PHYSICAL|NON_PRIVILEGED (flags 0x48, ogkm-580 g_dispsw_nvoc.c:181-189), so it would arrive as a GSP RmControl. Nothing in crates/ handles it on either branch (git grep: 0 hits), so it would show up as a `GSP REFUSED fn76/0x90720101` line, the way 69 other refused controls do at their first_seq. Run 10 has none. Lever: none today. If a client ever sends it, serve it from the register drainer by queueing a one-shot callback to the display worker, which writes the notifier at the next timer tick (never on a vCPU, never under the GSP lock). Until then keep the by-name refusal and its counter (V3_DISPLAY.md on v3-dispsw-exp:374-380).

THREE DOCUMENTED PREMISES ARE CONTRADICTED BY THESE MEASUREMENTS. (a) OWNER_RULINGS.md §M (origin/master docs/OWNER_RULINGS.md:369-371, 375-376): 'host RM owns the release timing' and 'vsync'd X11 clients would then run uncapped' on a headless host. Measured on the headless GA106: vsync 59.2-59.8 against no-vsync 2716 (lane.log:149-150). (b) V3_DISPLAY.md (v3-dispsw-exp):284-285 says vsync is paced 'by its flips'. Bare-X windowed has 0 flips; it is the vblank interrupt. (c) kf-disp model.rs:142-145 and V3_DISPLAY.md (v3-dispsw-exp):425 say GL with display-SW REFUSED is 'vsync-locked at 60 FPS'. Every off run's own no-vsync control equals its vsync number: m3f 57.4/57.4, m3h 54.1/53.5, m3z 56.3/58.7 (origin/master traces/v3_display/m3*_20260930/hook/glxgears*.log), run 9 56.4-57.6/59.0, runs 1/5/7 ~40/~40, and broker run brkA3 82.5 FPS (runA3.log:118). Off-mode GL is not vsync-paced; something unexplained caps it at 40-82.

THE REAL LEVER: kf-disp's vblank period. One knob covers KMS flips, fullscreen X flips, compositor flips (Cinnamon: updates/releases/scanouts ≈ +120 per 2 s while glxgears ran) and windowed X11 GL/VK FIFO (via the guest's vblank interrupt and the RG frame counter). The period comes from the armed raster (display.rs:2032-2061 broker; logged as `head 3 ACTIVE raster 2200x1125 period 16666 us`). It lives in the worker-owned `next_vblank` (display.rs:1568, deadline 1593-1606), so changing it is arithmetic on the worker thread. It cannot block a vCPU and takes no lock, which meets THE_CONSTRAINTS §6/§25 and the two lock-free blocking points (origin/master docs/design/THE_CONSTRAINTS.md:79, 163-185, 860-875).

EDID LIMITS ON 'THE PREFERRED MODE FOLLOWS THE SAME RATE'. Monitor::for_window clamps the refresh to 24-75 Hz (origin/v3-broker crates/kf-disp/src/edid.rs:179-183). If the pixel clock exceeds max_pixel_khz (165 000 kHz default, display.rs:2112-2116), it silently shrinks the resolution by 15/16 steps (edid.rs:185-198), and 1080p CVT-RB at 75 Hz already exceeds 165 MHz. So display-max-fps above ~60 at 1080p would lower the resolution, and values outside 24-75 cannot be expressed through EDID at all. Either refuse such values by name, or decouple: period = max(raster period, 1/cap), with the decoupled case's effect on guest timestamp maths unmeasured.

DOORBELL PACING — I'd not build it, for five measured or cited reasons. (1) Passthrough doorbells ring the host inline on the vCPU by owner ruling: 'passthrough doorbells are inline in vcpu, no queue, no worker' (origin/v3-dispsw-exp crates/kf-trap/src/trap.rs:128-132). A pacer needs a new queued route plus a worker timer. (2) The twin is born over the guest's own GPFIFO VA and USERD (crates/kf-qemu/src/chan.rs:22-27), so the host engine reads the guest's GP_PUT directly; holding back the doorbell may not hold back the work. An older tree measured exactly this: 'the hardware fetches without a doorbell from us' (origin/master docs/archive/w266_completion_pin_prereg.md:33-38). (3) With doorbell-ioeventfd=on, the drainer rings inline and must never hold 'a timer' (crates/kf-chan/src/dbfast.rs:15-19). (4) Doorbells per frame vary by path (run 10 qemu.log DOORBELL-LEDGER): Cinnamon glxgears 2469 in a 15 s run (~2.8/frame, line 3882), no-vsync 84055 (~2.6, line 4278), bare-X windowed 1348 (~1.9, line 9900), fullscreen 1338 (~1.9, line 10267), Cinnamon vkcube exactly 4/frame (960 for --c 240, lines 5177 and 6935; 4800 for --c 1200, line 8119), bare-X vkcube FIFO exactly 3/frame (1440 for --c 480, line 11163). A doorbell cap is therefore not a frame cap. (5) 'Channels owning a display-SW object' include the X server's 2D channel (twins on host 0x2a, lines 2260-2273; tok 0x3 rung=3720, line 9259) and the compositor's (host 0x2c, tok 0x5 rung=8947, line 9093), so pacing them throttles all X drawing.

DELAYING A HOST-SIDE RELEASE is not a lever. None happened on the measured stack (dsw_calls=0), and the release would run inside host CPU-RM and GSP (kernel_gsp.c:1109-1135), where kayfabe has no hook.

UNMEASURED RISK: a host whose GPU drives a monitor. Every twin is authored with head 0 (`authored: head 0, displayMask 0, caps 0`, qemu.log 'act display-SW twin' lines). If GSP's handling of the guest's methods waits for host head 0's vblank, an active host head would add a second clock on top of kf-disp's: a cap at the host's refresh, or beating against it. The README lists this as not shown (dispsw_20261003/README.md 'Not shown here'). Test on a box with a live host head; the broker box runs host Xorg on the NVIDIA GPU at 1920x1080 (broker_20261003/brkA/prep.log). Set the guest to 50 Hz and the host to 60 Hz, then compare glxgears with kfdsw `dsw_calls`. If the host clock shows through, a possible fix is to author an inactive host head (needs measuring).

A FIXED COPY CLOCK CAPS WHAT THE HOST SEES. A front-buffer X11 window with no compositor reaches the console or broker only at refresh_due's rate: 33 ms (30 Hz) when watched, 250 ms (4 Hz) otherwise (origin/v3-broker display.rs:2453-2466; v3-dispsw-exp display.rs:1990-1997). In run 10 the 59.5 FPS bare-X glxgears produced only +48 scanouts in ~12 s (3776→3824, ≈4 Hz). display-max-fps=60 is therefore not what a viewer gets on this path. Owner call: should this clock follow the bound, at ~1.2 ms GPU copy each (scanout_avg_us=1200)?

FALSIFIER BEFORE PROMISING ANYTHING (decisive, and no new mechanism needed): drive the existing resize path request_ui(0, w, h, refresh_mhz) → apply_ui_request → Monitor::for_window → hotplug (origin/v3-broker display.rs:1322-1334, 2105-2133). Do one run at 30 Hz (1920x1080) and one at 50-75 Hz (1280x720, inside 165 MHz), and confirm `period 33333 us` (or similar) in the kf3 log. Prediction if kf-disp's timer is the pacer: bare-X windowed glxgears ≈30 / ≈50-75 FPS, and vkcube FIFO --c 480 lasting ≈16 s / ≈6.4-9.6 s (raise the hook's `timeout 12`). If the FPS stays at 60, the attribution is wrong and the NOTIFY and doorbell questions reopen.

IDENTIFY THE GUEST CONSUMER (kayfabe cannot see it). GET_VBLANK_COUNTER 0x730105 has flags 0x8 and is handled in the guest's own CPU-RM (ogkm-580 g_disp_objs_nvoc.c:2919-2923). Each call registers a persistent vblank callback with a 5 s keepalive (disp_common_kern_ctrl_minimal.c:338-399; vblank.h:78), which would produce exactly the observed 'interrupts on for the client's lifetime'. The other candidate is NVKMS's NV9010 callback (vblank_callback.c:53-108). To decide between them, run guest-side kretprobes, the same technique as scripts/bench/display/kfdsw_probe/kfdsw_probe.c, on kheadAddVblankCallback_IMPL, dispcmnCtrlCmdSystemGetVblankCounter_IMPL and vblcbConstruct_IMPL, counted by process name. Alternatively run glxgears and Xorg under /workspace/nvidia-gpu-passthrough/tests/mode2/nvdiff/nvdiff_shim.c. Passthrough pushbuffers must not be parsed by kayfabe (owner ruling, 2026-09-08), so counting display-SW methods has to be done on the guest side.

STATUS-LINE DESIGN, ACHIEVED RATE PER PATH (each a 2 s rate from counters the worker or the vCPU already keeps; no new trap work): `pace[bound=<cfg> vblank_hz[h] flip_hz[h] vbl_irq_hz[h] front_copy_hz db_hz_dsw=<max over display-SW channels> dsw_chans=N]`. flip_hz is exact for KMS and fullscreen X. vbl_irq_hz, counted while updates is flat, is the windowed path's clock. front_copy_hz is what a viewer sees for no-compositor windows. db_hz_dsw counts submissions, not frames (measured 1.9-4 per frame). Its source is the per-token doorbell atomics the vCPU already writes (chan.rs:949), snapshotted by the status thread; with the fast path on, the FastLedger counts (dbfast.rs:103-120) need a periodic read. # display-max-fps: implementable design

I checked both investigations against the source. The design is read against `origin/v3-broker` 65394eac, `origin/v3-dispsw-exp` 86b4fa10 and `origin/master` 789dee9f. Broker 65394eac changes only docs and traces since c38032f3, so its code is the same as c38032f3.

Prefixes used below: B = v3-broker, D = v3-dispsw-exp, M = master, O = `/workspace/nvidia-gpu-passthrough/research_clones/ogkm-580.159.04`.

## How the display is going (for the user's question)

- **KMS flips:** paced by kf-disp's own vblank tick. Measured 59.95 Hz (B `traces/v3_display/broker_20261003/brkA/run_brkA_qemu_excerpt.log:52`).
- **X11 with x11-dispsw=on:** works.
  - Cinnamon up, X11 vkcube exits 0.
  - vsync glxgears runs at 59.2-59.8 FPS; with vsync off it runs at 2716 FPS (D `traces/v3_display/dispsw_20261003/10_b_on_d84086df/lane.log:149-150`).
  - Host CPU-RM's release path was entered 0 times (`lane.log:172`).
- **`0x90720101`:** never sent (D `dispsw_20261003/README.md:102`, `:153`).
- **display-max-fps:** not built on any branch (B `docs/design/V3_DISPLAY.md:2577`, `:2643`).
- **§M's X11 premise is contradicted.** §M (M `docs/OWNER_RULINGS.md:369-371`) says host RM owns release timing, so vsync'd X11 clients would run uncapped on a headless host. They do not run uncapped.
  - In run 10, bare-X windowed glxgears made 0 flips: `updates` stayed at 3219.
  - Over the same span the guest took about 60 display interrupts a second: `irqs` 6717→7399, `vblanks` 10742→11471 (D `…/10_b_on_d84086df/run_fin_on_d84086df_qemu.log:9672`, `:9963`).
  - So kf-disp's tick is very likely the X11 pacer too. This is a correlation until run R2/R3 below confirms it.

## 1. The property

- **Name:** `display-max-fps`, a QEMU `DEFINE_PROP_UINT32` in whole Hz, default 0.
  - 0 means "follow the virtual monitor".
  - The ABI word is Hz, so C never multiplies and there is no overflow path. All rates in the code are already whole Hz: `for_window` rounds mHz to Hz at B `crates/kf-disp/src/edid.rs:179-183`.
- **Validation:** done in Rust `Config::check`, before anything is opened. This follows D `crates/kf-qemu/src/device.rs:66-81`: "a property that silently does nothing is refused by name". Refused cases:
  - Non-zero without `display=on`.
  - Below 24: the floor of `Timing::cvt_rb` (edid.rs:85) and of the EDID range-limits minimum.
  - Above 75: the single-link 165 MHz DVI connector (`kf-disp/src/model.rs:916-931`) cannot carry it. Going above 75 needs a dual-link or HDMI connector, which is not built.
- **The effective bound is one number: the rate the virtual monitor was authored for (`rate_hz`).** It is both the EDID preferred refresh and the tick clamp. The configured value only caps the monitor.
  - `pace::monitor_rate(cfg_hz, surface_mhz)`:
    - (0, 0) → 60, source "default"
    - (0, S) → S, source "host"
    - (B, 0) → B, source "cfg"
    - (B, S) → min(B, S)
  - The host value S is rounded to Hz, then clamped to 24..=75.
  - The rate is then fitted to the requested size (§5). The bound is `rate_hz × 1000` mHz, so it is never above what the EDID advertises.

## 2. The one mechanism: the clamped vblank tick

**Where the tick lives today.** The `kf3-display` worker's epoll deadline is the tick; there is deliberately no timerfd (B `crates/kf-linux-raw/src/lib.rs:239-244`).
- Deadline: B `crates/kf-qemu/src/display.rs:1593-1616`.
- Step 4, the tick itself: `:1750-1787`.
- The period is armed from the guest's raster with no clamp: `:2032-2064` from `engine.rs:1058-1091`.

**The change.** Add a pure helper:
```rust
paced_period_ns(raster_ns, bound_mhz) =
    if raster_ns == 0 { 0 } else { raster_ns.max(1_000_000_000_000 / bound_mhz) }
```
- It uses floor division, so CEA 1080p60 is a no-op: the raster gives 16 666 666 ns and so does 1e12/60000.
- Arming goes through `pace::vblank_slot(prev, raster_ns, bound_mhz, now)`, which replaces `display.rs:2039-2048`.
- The phase check must compare against the **clamped** period, not the raster (`:2041`). Otherwise every Heads effect re-phases the tick.
- `heads_armed()` stays truthful. `period_ns > 0` is also the "head lit" test at `engine.rs:836`, `:940`, `:1126` and `display.rs:1800`, `:1813`, `:2187`.
- When the bound changes (`apply_ui_request`, below), the worker re-arms the active heads with the same helper.

**Precision.** The average rate is exact. Each tick can be up to about 1 ms late: `PollTimeout::Millis` floors the wait and applies `max(1)` (`display.rs:1612-1616`). Ticks reschedule from the scheduled time (`:1764-1768`).

**Hostile guests.** A guest that programs a 1 kHz raster today gets about 1 kHz of ticks and interrupts per head. With the clamp it gets the bound.

| Path | Mechanism | Exactness |
|---|---|---|
| Non-tearing KMS flips: Wayland, nvidia-drm, fullscreen X via NVKMS, compositor flips | Parked until the head's tick (`engine.rs:816-863`); completions wait for the scanout copy (`display.rs:1898-1916`) | Exact: at most the bound per head, +1 per 1 s window |
| Guest vblank consumers: NVKMS vblank callbacks and vblank-semaphore control (O `src/nvidia-modeset/src/nvkms-vblank-sem-control.c:66`), the RG_DPCA frame counter, the HEAD_TIMING interrupt | Driven by the same tick (`display.rs:1770-1786`) | Exact |
| Tearing / async KMS flips | The new tearing gate (§3) | Exact upper bound; slower clients are untouched |
| X11 display-SW (windowed GLX, X11 Vulkan FIFO) with x11-dispsw=on | The guest's vblank interrupt from the same tick (run 10 correlation) | **Expected, not promised.** Graded in the guest by R2/R3 |
| X11 GL with x11-dispsw=off | None. vsync is unavailable ("Failed to allocate display software resources") | **Not bounded.** brkA3 ran glxgears at 82.5 FPS on a 60 Hz monitor (B `…/brkA2_brkA3/runA3.log:118`) |
| Frames shown on the host (console and broker) | Flip copies follow the tick; non-flip copies are gated (§4); the broker's EV_FRAME credit sits downstream and never paces the guest (`display.rs:444-450`, runA3.log:118) | At most the tick rate, +1 at transitions |

## 3. Tearing gate (pure engine change; needs owner decision D1)

- **Why it is needed.** nvidia-drm enables async flips (O `kernel-open/nvidia-drm/nvidia-drm-drv.c:386-388`) and maps them to `tearing=TRUE` (`nvidia-drm-crtc.c:1656-1667`). NVKMS then programs `BEGIN_MODE_IMMEDIATE` (`src/nvidia-modeset/src/nvkms-evo3.c:3954-3960`). The engine parks only `NON_TEARING` flips (`engine.rs:831-843`), so async flips latch at once. Today they are limited only by one copy in flight (`display.rs:1928`).
- **Gate state.** `Engine` gains `tear_gate: bool` (default true) and a per-head `presented: [bool; 8]` flag.
- **Rule in `group_ready`.** If a group with no core member contains a non-NON_TEARING window on an active head `h`, and `presented[h]` is already set, park the group at `h` and count `tear_held[h] += 1`.
- **Setting and clearing the flag.**
  - Any window-flip latch on `h` sets it, whether it happened at a tick or immediately.
  - `vblank(h)` clears it **before** latching parked groups (`engine.rs:588-596`).
- **Result.**
  - At most one window-flip present per head per tick interval.
  - A client that is already slower than the bound still latches at once and tears as it asked.
  - No time source is involved and no new timer is needed.
- **New public counters**, next to `updates` and `methods` (`engine.rs:460-467`), all per head:
  - `presents[h]`: ticks that latched at least one window, plus tearing latches.
  - `tearing[h]`
  - `tear_held[h]`

## 4. Copies made without a flip (fixes §O "coalesced to the display rate", which is not built)

- Today the refresh clock is fixed: 33 ms watched, 250 ms unwatched (`display.rs:2457-2467`). Cursor moves and mode switches start a copy at once (`:1887-1897`).
- **Proposed gate:**
  ```rust
  pace::copy_gate(want, flip_pending = scan.barrier > scan.started, scan.last, gap, now)
      -> Start | WaitUntil(t) | Idle
  ```
  - `gap = max(1/bound, the console head's paced period)`.
  - Flip copies are never gated; they are already tick-paced, and gating them would delay completions.
  - A `WaitUntil` time joins the deadline minimum at `:1603-1605`.
- **Refresh clock:** `pace::refresh_every(watched, gap) = if watched { max(33 ms, gap) } else { 250 ms }`. Unwatched copies stay at 250 ms; watched ones at 30 Hz or the bound if lower. The refresh clock is never above the bound.

## 5. EDID and monitor

- **`Monitor` gains two fields:**
  - `rate_hz`: the bound's source.
  - `max_v_hz`: the range-limit maximum, today hard-coded 75 at `edid.rs:259-263`.
- **`kf_rm::display::monitors(max_fps_hz)`** replaces `monitors()` (B `crates/kf-rm/src/display.rs:124-127`). It feeds both the GOP (`kf-qemu/src/device.rs:263-267`) and `model_for` (`kf-rm/src/display.rs:132-138`), so the GOP and the model "cannot disagree".
  - Unset: `default_1080p()`, **byte-identical** to today's EDID, range 24..75.
  - Set: `for_window(1920, 1080, B·1000, 165 000)` with `max_v_hz = rate_hz`.
- **When `rate_hz < 60`, drop every 60 Hz extra:** established timings (`edid.rs:241-243`), standard timings (`:244-257`), and the second CEA DTD (`:271-279`). Otherwise NVKMS keeps EDID-listed modes even when the EDID's own range excludes them (O `src/nvidia-modeset/src/nvkms-modepool.c:1472-1490`).
- **`for_window` yields the rate, not the size, above 60 Hz.**
  - It picks the highest Hz in 60..=target that fits the clock at the requested size. Only if none fits does it fall back to today's size-shrink loop (`edid.rs:186-198`).
  - At 1080p, CVT-RB is 164 750 kHz at 71 Hz and 167 250 kHz at 72 Hz (computed with `edid.rs:84-126`). So a 72-75 Hz request gives 1920x1080@71, not 1800x1012.
  - This fixes a latent broker bug that exists independently of §M.
  - Behaviour at 60 Hz and below is unchanged.
- **`apply_ui_request`** (`display.rs:2105-2133`, already on the worker under the model lock):
  - computes the target with `pace::monitor_rate(dp.max_fps_hz, mhz)`;
  - returns the new `rate_hz`, so the worker updates its cached bound;
  - takes nothing new per tick.
- **Relay de-duplication.** `kf-broker/src/conn.rs:1687-1690` drops a SURFACE whose size is unchanged, so a refresh-only change never reaches the guest. It must de-duplicate on (w, h, mhz). The field is at `:395` and the pin is `tests/relay_machine.rs:955-957`.
- Worked values: 1080p@30 CVT-RB is 68 250 kHz, giving 29.94 Hz and a 33 402 µs period. At 50 Hz it is 115 000 kHz, giving 49.99 Hz.

## 6. Levers §M names that are not built

- **`NOTIFY_ON_VBLANK` (`0x90720101`).**
  - It was called 0 times, and nothing in `crates/` on either branch handles it (grep finds 0 hits). Keep the by-name refusal and its counter (D `V3_DISPLAY.md:374-380`).
  - kf-disp cannot service it alone. The semaphore and notifier it reports into are bound by display-SW methods on a passthrough channel, and kayfabe must not parse those (D `crates/kf-qemu/src/chan.rs:22-27`). Only GSP sees them; CPU-RM has no implementation (O `g_dispsw_nvoc.h:450-452`).
  - If a client ever sends it: the drainer queues it to the worker, which forwards it to the host twin at the next clamped tick (step 4). It must never be handled on a vCPU or under the GSP lock. On a headless host, RM then runs the callback immediately (O `src/nvidia/src/kernel/gpu/disp/vblank_callback/vblank.c:87-90`, `:209-243`).
- **Pacing display-SW doorbells.** Rejected unless R2/R3 fail. Reasons:
  1. Passthrough doorbells are rung inline on the vCPU by owner ruling (D `crates/kf-trap/src/trap.rs:128-132`). Pacing would mean blocking the vCPU (§6/§25) or adding a queued route.
  2. The twin reads GP_PUT from the guest's own USERD, so holding the doorbell may not hold the work. An older tree measured exactly that (M `docs/archive/w266_completion_pin_prereg.md:33-38`).
  3. The fast-path drainer may not hold a timer (D `crates/kf-chan/src/dbfast.rs:15-19`).
  4. Doorbells per frame vary from 1.9 to 4 by path (run 10 DOORBELL-LEDGER), so a doorbell cap is not a frame cap.
  5. The X server and compositor channels own display-SW objects too, so pacing them would throttle all X drawing.

## 7. Status line

- **The worker owns a `pace::Meter`.** Each pass it reads the engine counters, the per-head tick count, `vblirq` (incremented when `head_timing_en[h] & head_vblank` is set; `ports.rs:52`, `display.rs:1782-1786`), and copy counts.
- Every 1 s (or more) it publishes milli-rates to `DispCounters` atomics. `status_line` reads them without a lock.
- **Fragment**, placed directly after `disp[...]` (B `device.rs:2258-2284`):
  ` fps[bound=30.000(cfg) h0:tick=29.94,kms=29.9,tear=0.0,held=0,vblirq=29.9 copies=29.9 front=0.0 kms_max=30.0 over=0]`
  - Only lit heads are printed.
  - `over` counts 1 s windows where a head's presents exceeded `bound × elapsed + 1`. It is always printed, even at 0.
  - **Placement matters.** kf3.c truncates the realize and exit lines at 4096 bytes (B `qemu/hw/misc/kf3/kf3.c:1286`, `:1295`), and run 10's heartbeat line is already 4275 bytes. Putting the fragment early keeps `over` out of the truncated tail.
- **dispsw build only:** inside `dispsw[...]` (D `chan.rs:2540`), add `db_hz_max=` and `db_chans=`.
  - These are per-token trap doorbell deltas over the channels that own display-SW twins, using the existing `rung` atomics (D `chan.rs:950`, `:1362-1375`).
  - The previous snapshot is kept in a Mutex used only by the status thread.
  - They count submissions, not frames. With doorbell-ioeventfd=on the line prints `db=fast-unmeasured` (`FastLedger` is only readable at deregister, `dbfast.rs:103-120`).

## 8. Constraints check

- vCPU path: unchanged (a PUT is one atomic plus an eventfd, `display.rs:1238-1243`).
- Pacing is deadline arithmetic in the worker's epoll wait, one of the two lock-free blocking points (M `docs/design/THE_CONSTRAINTS.md:860-862`), and satisfies §6 (`:79-83`) and §25 (`:163-185`).
- The model lock is taken only in the existing `apply_ui_request`, never per tick.
- Parking a tearing flip is engine state, not a wait.

## 9. Tests that can fail without a GPU, and the mutation each one catches

1. `paced_period_is_the_slower_of_raster_and_bound` (pace). Cases:
   - (16 666 666, 60 000) → itself
   - (1 000 000, 60 000) → 16 666 666
   - (33 402 197, 60 000) → itself
   - raster 0 → 0
   - bound 0 → no clamp

   Catches: `min` for `max`; ceil instead of floor (CEA stops being a no-op); dropping the zero guard (an idle head lights up).
2. `vblank_slot_keeps_phase_under_the_clamp`. Previous slot (t, 16.67 ms) with a 1 ms raster at bound 60 returns the same t.
   Catches: comparing against the raster (as `:2041` does today) re-phases the tick.
3. `monitor_rate_table`. Expected (input → output):
   - (0, 0) → 60
   - (30, 60 000) → 30
   - (75, 60 000) → 60
   - (0, 59 940) → 60
   - (0, 23 000) → 24

   Catches: `max` for `min`; ignoring S.
4. `config_check_refuses_by_name`.
   - Accepted: 0, 24, 60 and 75 with display on.
   - Refused, naming `display-max-fps`: 23, 76, and 60 with display off.

   Catches: off-by-one range limits; a missing display check.
5. `the_unset_edid_is_byte_identical`. `monitors(0)[0].edid()` equals a golden array taken at the pre-change commit.
   Catches: writing `max_v` = 60 when unset.
6. `a_bound_below_60_lists_no_60hz_mode`. For `monitors(30)`:
   - bytes 35..38 are 0;
   - the standard timings are all `[1,1]`;
   - bytes 108..112 are the dummy descriptor;
   - byte 78 is 30;
   - the preferred refresh is at most 30.

   Catches: forgetting any one of the three extras.
7. `above_71hz_the_rate_yields_not_the_size`. `for_window(1920, 1080, 75 000, 165 000)` gives 1920x1080 with `rate_hz` 71 and a clock of at most 165 000 kHz. `(3840, 2160, 60 000)` stays as today.
   Catches: today's shrink-first loop.
8. `every_authored_edid_contains_its_preferred_mode`. Sweep B ∈ {0, 24..=75} × S ∈ {0, 24..=240 Hz}. Each EDID must satisfy:
   - the preferred mode lies inside the range limits;
   - its clock ≤ max pixel clock;
   - the checksum is valid;
   - its refresh ≤ `rate_hz`.

   Catches: `rate_hz` taken from the target before fitting.
9. `a_second_tearing_flip_waits_for_the_vblank` (`engine/tests.rs`, using the helpers at `:20-67`). On an active head:
   - #1 IMMEDIATE latches at once;
   - #2 parks (GET before its UPDATE, `waiting()`);
   - `vblank` latches #2;
   - #3 parks;
   - `vblank` latches #3;
   - an idle `vblank` passes;
   - #4 latches at once.

   Catches:
   - not clearing the flag in `vblank` (#4 parks);
   - not setting it on a tick latch (#3 latches at once);
   - gating inactive heads (the existing `flips_without_an_active_head_latch_at_once`, `:337`, fails);
   - with `tear_gate = false`, nothing parks.
10. `presents_count_one_per_tick`. Two windows latched by one `vblank` count `presents = 1`.
    Catches: counting per window.
11. `meter_over`.
    - 60 presents in 1.000 s at bound 60 → over 0.
    - 61 → 0.
    - 62 → 1.
    - Elapsed 1.05 s with 63 presents → 0.

    Catches: dropping the +1 tolerance; dividing by a fixed 1 s instead of the measured elapsed time.
12. `copy_gate`.
    - A pending flip → Start, even 1 ms after the last copy.
    - A non-flip copy inside the gap → WaitUntil(last + gap).
    - After the gap → Start.
    - `refresh_every(true, 33.3 ms)` → 33.3 ms.

    Catches: gating flip copies; `min` in `refresh_every`.
13. `relay_machine.rs`: add `EV_SURFACE 1600×900 @30 000` after the 59 940 one and expect a second `Input::Surface`.
    Catches: de-duplicating on size only.
14. `db_rate`. A token whose counter resets on reuse gives a delta of `cur`, not a wrapped value.
    Catches: `wrapping_sub`.
15. `wire_mirror.rs` (existing, `:116`, `:415`). It fails if `kf3.h` and `ffi_unsafe::kf3_realize` disagree on the new word or the ABI number.

# display-max-fps: revised design

## 1. The property

**Definition.** `display-max-fps` is a `DEFINE_PROP_UINT32` in whole Hz, default 0. The ABI word is in Hz, so C never multiplies.

**Validation.** `Config::check` refuses the following by name, following the existing `check` pattern at D `device.rs:66-77`:
- a non-zero value without `display=on`;
- a value below 24, the floor of `cvt_rb` (B `edid.rs:85`);
- a value above 75, kayfabe's authoring ceiling (`for_window` clamps at B `edid.rs:182`; the range-limit maximum is at `:262`; going higher is owner decision D3).

**Two numbers (replaces the reviewed design's single `monitor_rate`):**
- **`cap_hz`** is B, or **75** when B is unset. It stays the same for the whole life of the device and is the hard ceiling on every head's tick. When unset, 75 is the most any EDID kayfabe authors can advertise, so the cap never contradicts a mode the monitor offers.
- **`preferred_hz(B, S)`** gives the EDID's preferred refresh. S is rounded to Hz and clamped to 24–75 (S = 0 means no host rate). Then it is fitted to the requested size (§5).

| B (cfg) | S (host) | preferred_hz |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 60 |
| 0 | S | S |
| B | 0 | B |
| B | S | min(B, S) |

**EDID range.** The range-limit maximum (`max_v_hz`) equals `cap_hz`. When unset that is 75, so today's EDID stays byte-identical.

**Invariant: no DTD the EDID lists runs faster than the cap.**
- The 60 Hz established and standard timings (VESA DMT, up to 60.317 Hz for 800x600) are listed only when cap ≥ 60.
- NVKMS accepts non-EDID modes up to 1.01 × the cap (O `nvkms-modepool.c:1447-1448`).
- So the clamp can slow a mode the guest validly chose by at most 1%, or at most 0.53% for a listed DMT mode at cap = 60.
- Beyond that it applies only when the guest overrides validation (O `nvkms-api.h:348`, `:356`; `nvkms-modepool.c:1432`). That case shows as `clamped=1`.

## 2. The mechanism: a clamped vblank tick

**Where the tick lives today.** It is the worker's epoll deadline (B `display.rs:1593-1616`; there is deliberately no timerfd, B `crates/kf-linux-raw/src/lib.rs:239-244`). Each tick runs at B `display.rs:1750-1787`.

**The change.** A new `kf_disp::pace::Pacer { cap_mhz, slots: [Option<(u64 at_ns, u64 period_ns)>; 8] }` owns what is now `next_vblank` (B `display.rs:1568`).
- `period = if raster == 0 { 0 } else { raster.max(1e12 / cap_mhz) }`, using floor division.
- `Pacer::on_heads(&[HeadMode], now)` replaces B `display.rs:2038-2048`. It compares the *clamped* period in its phase check.
- `Pacer::due(now)` replaces the slot loop at `:1752-1768` and keeps today's late-tick rule.
- Because the cap is constant, there is no re-arm path for when the bound changes.
- `heads_armed()` stays truthful: `period_ns > 0` remains the "head lit" test at B `engine.rs:836`, `:940`, `:1126`.

**Log line.** It becomes `head N ACTIVE raster WxH period <ns> ns (raster <ns> ns, cap <Hz>)`, printed in nanoseconds so it is not truncated (F5).

**Precision.**
- The long-run average is at most the cap. Floor division makes it 0.04 ppm high.
- In any window of length L there are at most floor(L·r) + 2 ticks, because of the late-tick rule (F3).
- The worst lateness is published as `late_max_us`. That includes worker stalls, such as the instance-memory `zero_store` at B `display.rs:1630-1636`.

**Hostile guests.** Today a 1 kHz raster gives about 1 kHz of interrupts per head. After the change a head gets at most `cap_hz` (75 when unset).

**Bounds by path:**

| Path | Mechanism | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| Non-tearing window flips in groups without the core | Parked until the head's tick (B `engine.rs:822-843`); completions wait for the copy (B `display.rs:1898-1916`) | At most floor(L·r) + 2 |
| Window flips interlocked with the core | Latch at once (B `engine.rs:842-843`) | **Not bounded.** Counted as `core_imm` and included in `presents` and `over` |
| Tearing (async) flips | Tearing gate, §3 | At most floor(L·r) + 2 |
| Guest vblank consumers: NVKMS callbacks, vblank-semaphore control, the RG_DPCA frame count, the HEAD_TIMING interrupt | Driven by the tick (B `display.rs:1770-1786`) | Same as the tick |

| X11 with vsync off | None | Not bounded on any path (2716 FPS, `lane.log:150`) |
| X11 with x11-dispsw=off | No vsync | Not bounded (82.5 FPS, B `traces/v3_display/broker_20261003/brkA2_brkA3/runA3.log:118`) |

## 3. Tearing gate (owner decision D1)

**Why it is needed.** nvidia-drm's async flips latch at once today. They are limited only by having one copy in flight (B `display.rs:1928`).

**State.** `Engine` gains `tear_gate` (default true), a per-head `presented[h]` flag, and per-head counters `presents`, `tearing`, `tear_held` and `core_imm`.

**Rule in `group_ready`.** A group without the core that holds a tearing window on an active head h parks at h if `presented[h]` is set.

**Setting and clearing the flag.**
- It is set in `latch_group` when at least one window owned by h was actually completed. It is not set on parking, and not when an unmet acquire stops the latch.
- `vblank(h)` clears it before latching.

**`presents` is counted per `latch_group` call**, wherever the latch happens. That covers latches at a tick, immediate latches and core-group latches (F3).

**New: release on idle (F7).** `Engine::head_idle(h)` latches every group parked at h. The worker calls it when `on_heads` turns h idle.

**Cost.** A parked tearing flip with an unmet acquire waits for the next tick instead of the 2 ms acquire poll (B `display.rs:1600`). That adds at most one tick of latency and causes no block.

## 4. Copies made without a flip

- `pace::copy_gate(want, flip_pending = scan.barrier > scan.started, last, gap, now)` returns `Start`, `WaitUntil(t)` or `Idle`.

  - `WaitUntil` joins the deadline at B `display.rs:1603-1605`.
- `refresh_every(watched, gap)` is `max(33 ms, gap)` when watched and 250 ms otherwise. Today's fixed values are at B `display.rs:2457-2467`.
- Non-flip copies never hold completions, because only a flip moves `barrier` (B `display.rs:1903`).

## 5. EDID and monitor

**`Monitor` gains two fields:**
- `rate_hz`: the preferred rate.
- `max_v_hz`: equal to `cap_hz`. Today it is hard-coded to 75 at B `edid.rs:259-263`.

**`kf_rm::display::monitors(cfg_hz)`** replaces B `crates/kf-rm/src/display.rs:124-127`, and `model_for` takes the same value (`:132-138`). The GOP (B `device.rs:263-267`, `gop.rs:187`) and the model still read one source.

**When cap < 60, drop every 60 Hz extra:**
- the established timings (B `edid.rs:241-243`);

**`apply_ui_request`** (B `display.rs:2105-2133`) passes `preferred_hz(B, mhz)` as the target. It does not re-arm the tick.

**Relay de-duplication.** The broker drops SURFACE events whose size is unchanged (B `conn.rs:1687-1690`; the field is at `:395`). It must de-duplicate on (w, h, mhz) instead.

## 6. Levers §M names that stay unbuilt

**`NOTIFY_ON_VBLANK` (`0x90720101`).**
- Keep the refusal by name and its counter (D `docs/design/V3_DISPLAY.md:374-380`). **Do not forward it** (F2).
- Servicing it would need one of two things, and neither is allowed under current constraints:
  - kernel-mapped notifier memory, which the branch removed;
  - reading display-SW methods that kayfabe must not parse (D `chan.rs:22-27`).
- ⚠ A refusal on a wait path can act as a forged completion. If a client ever calls it, check how that client treats `NOT_SUPPORTED` before anything else.

**Pacing display-SW doorbells.** Rejected for the reviewed design's five reasons, all verified (see the findings). The 1.9–4 doorbells per frame figure comes from the run-10 DOORBELL-LEDGER.

## 7. Status

- **The worker owns a `pace::Meter`.** Every 1 s or more it publishes milli-rates to `DispCounters` atomics.
- **It prints its own line**, at most every 2 s and only when something changed. Being a separate line, it escapes the 4096-byte truncation at B `kf3.c:1286` and `:1295`:
  ```
  kf3: display fps cap=30(cfg) h0[armed=29.938 tick=29.94 clamped=0 late_max_us=812 kms=29.9 tear=0.0 held=0 core_imm=0 vblirq=29.9] copies=29.9 over=0
  ```
  The same fragment goes early in `status_line`, directly after `disp[...]` (B `device.rs:2258-2284`).
- **`over`** counts windows of at least 1 s where `presents > floor(tick_rate × elapsed) + 2`, using the measured elapsed time. It is always printed.
- **`vblirq`** counts ticks while `head_timing_en[h] & head_vblank` is set (B `ports.rs:52`). It is a precondition indicator (a vblank consumer is active), not a grade.
- **dispsw builds only:** `dispsw[... db_hz_max= db_chans=]`. These are doorbell deltas keyed on (token, twin identity), with the snapshot behind `try_lock`.
  - They count submissions, not frames.
  - `db=fast-unmeasured` when doorbell-ioeventfd is on (D `dbfast.rs:103-120`).
- **Stated in the docs:** the status line cannot show an X11 breach (F6).

## 8. Constraints check

- **vCPU path:** unchanged (B `display.rs:1225-1243`).
- **Pacing waits only on epoll deadlines**, one of the two lock-free blocking points (M `docs/design/THE_CONSTRAINTS.md:860-863`). This satisfies §6 (`:79-80`) and §25 (`:163-185`).
- **No new lock acquisitions.** The model lock per pass (B `display.rs:1622-1627`) and in `apply_ui_request` already exists (F10).
- **Parking is engine state, never a wait.** The existing 2 ms acquire poll (B `display.rs:1600`) gets no worse.
- **Guest-side vblank waits** read shadow registers (`read_exits=0` in run 10's status lines). At 24 Hz a guest busy-wait lasts at most 42 ms of guest CPU and holds no host lock.

## 9. Tests that can fail without a GPU (mutation each catches)

1. **`paced_period_is_the_slower_of_raster_and_bound`.** Cases: (16 666 666, 60 000) unchanged; (1 000 000, 60 000) → 16 666 666; raster 0 → 0. Catches `min` for `max`, ceil instead of floor, and a dropped zero guard.
2. **`on_heads_keeps_phase_under_the_clamp`.** Catches comparing against the raster, as B `display.rs:2041` does today.
3. **`preferred_and_cap_tables`.**
   - preferred_hz: (0,0)→60; (30, 60 000)→30; (75, 60 000)→60; (0, 59 940)→60; (0, 23 000)→24; (0, 144 000) at 1080p → 71.

4. **`config_check_refuses_by_name`.** Accepts 0, 24, 60 and 75; refuses 23, 76, and any value with display off.
5. **`the_unset_edid_is_byte_identical`** to a golden array taken at the pre-change commit.
6. **`a_cap_below_60_lists_no_60hz_mode`.** Bytes 35–37 are 0, the standard timings are all `[1,1]`, bytes 108–111 are the dummy descriptor, and byte 78 equals the cap.

8. **`every_authored_edid_honours_its_cap`.** Sweep B ∈ {0, 24..75} × S ∈ {0, 24..240}. Checks:
   - the preferred mode lies inside the range;
   - its clock is within the maximum pixel clock;

9. **`a_second_tearing_flip_waits_for_the_vblank`** (B `engine/tests.rs`, helpers at `:20-67`). Uses the reviewed design's sequence. Also confirms the existing `flips_without_an_active_head_latch_at_once` (`:337`) still passes.

11. **`a_group_parked_on_a_head_that_goes_idle_latches`.** Catches a missing `head_idle`.

13. **`meter_over`** at cap 60 over 1.000 s: 62 → 0, 63 → 1. Over 1.05 s, 64 → 0.
14. **`copy_gate`**, as in the reviewed design.
15. **`relay_machine.rs`:** adding `EV_SURFACE 1600×900 @30 000` yields a second `Input::Surface`.
16. **`db_rate_keyed_on_identity`.** Reuse where the new count is above the old snapshot gives the new count.
17. **`the_worker_arms_vblanks_only_through_the_pacer`.** A source scan of `display.rs` for any direct slot or period arithmetic, modelled on D `crates/kf-host/src/lib.rs:2049`. Catches a helper that is never called.
